title: Wall Street sees 3 AI futures. The same winners keep showing up.
excerpt: Morgan Stanley mapped 3 AI futures. Here's why Nvidia and the cloud giants could win no matter what happens.
content_html:
Morgan Stanley mapped 3 AI futures. One company wins them all.

By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Author of the Tech Memo newsletter

Will the AI future be closed or open, or a mixture of both? Morgan Stanley studied these three scenarios and found that some companies will win no matter what happens.

In a research note this week, the bank's strategists laid out three possible paths for the AI market over the next few years.

The winners change depending on which scenario plays out, but one theme stays remarkably consistent: The companies building the computing backbone that runs AI models and services will remain in a strong position regardless.

Closed wins

The first scenario is one where closed, proprietary AI models keep their lead. Companies continue paying a handful of frontier AI labs because they offer the best performance, security, and ease of use.

(The bank doesn't officially cover OpenAI and Anthropic, because they're still private companies, but I suspect these would be the main winners here).

This outcome would also favor major cloud providers including Amazon and Google, along with companies supplying the chips, networking equipment, and electricity needed to run massive AI systems, such as Nvidia and Bloom Energy.

A hybrid world

The second possibility is a hybrid world, which Morgan Stanley views as a realistic outcome. In my experience, these more nuanced outcomes are usually what ends up happening.

In this scenario, businesses would use premium, closed AI models for the hardest jobs while relying on cheaper, customizable models for routine work. That would spread AI across public clouds, private data centers, and company-owned hardware, creating opportunities for cloud providers, infrastructure software, and cybersecurity firms.

Winners would include hyperscale cloud providers such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft. Software companies including Datadog, Palantir, Crowdstrike, Okta, and ServiceNow would also do well in this world. Oh, and Nvidia, too.

Open wins

The third scenario assumes open models become just as capable and easy to use as proprietary ones. Lower costs would encourage companies to deploy AI much more broadly, with more workloads running inside their own data centers or on local devices instead of centralized cloud services.

That would benefit makers of enterprise hardware, security software, and so-called edge computing equipment which runs smaller systems closer to users.

Microsoft would still do well in this world, according to the Morgan Stanley strategists. But new winners would be Chinese AI labs and China's tech giants, such as MiniMax, Z.ai, Alibaba and Tencent.

Dell, HP, and Apple would also thrive in this scenario because they specialize in making devices that can run AI models and services closer to end users. Oh, and Nvidia wins again here.

Constant winners

Despite these very different outcomes, Morgan Stanley found some clear constants.

You've already spotted the clearest winner: Nvidia appears among the biggest beneficiaries in all three scenarios, reflecting the continued need for AI servers and networking no matter which type of software wins.

The cloud giants also feature prominently, although their rankings shift depending on whether proprietary or open models gain the upper hand. Microsoft stands out in the open-model scenario, while Amazon and Google are strongest if proprietary models remain dominant or the market settles into a hybrid approach.

Morgan Stanley's broader conclusion is that the debate over which type of AI model ultimately wins may matter less than many investors think.

If AI adoption continues to accelerate, the companies supplying the infrastructure that powers it could prosper in almost any future.

content_html_zh:
摩根士丹利绘制了 3 个人工智能期货。 一家公司赢得了所有这些。

作者：Alistair Barr 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 《技术备忘录》时事通讯的作者

人工智能的未来是封闭式的还是开放式的，还是两者兼而有之？ 摩根士丹利研究了这三种情况，发现无论发生什么，一些公司都会获胜。

在本周的一份研究报告中，该银行的策略师为未来几年的人工智能市场提出了三种可能的路径。

获胜者会根据具体情况而变化，但有一个主题保持非常一致：构建运行人工智能模型和服务的计算骨干的公司无论如何都将保持强势地位。

封闭式获胜

第一种情况是封闭的、专有的人工智能模型保持领先地位。 公司继续向一些前沿人工智能实验室付费，因为它们提供最佳的性能、安全性和易用性。

（该银行并未正式覆盖 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，因为它们仍然是私营公司，但我怀疑它们将是这里的主要赢家）。

这一结果也有利于包括亚马逊和谷歌在内的主要云提供商，以及提供运行大型人工智能系统所需的芯片、网络设备和电力的公司，例如英伟达和布鲁姆能源公司。

混合世界

第二种可能性是混合世界，摩根士丹利认为这是一个现实的结果。 根据我的经验，这些更微妙的结果通常是最终发生的。

在这种情况下，企业将使用优质、封闭的人工智能模型来完成最困难的工作，同时依靠更便宜、可定制的模型来完成日常工作。 这将把人工智能传播到公共云、私有数据中心和公司拥有的硬件上，为云提供商、基础设施软件和网络安全公司创造机会。

获胜者将包括亚马逊、谷歌和微软等超大规模云提供商。 Datadog、Palantir、Crowdstrike、Okta 和 ServiceNow 等软件公司也会在这个领域表现出色。 哦，还有英伟达。

公开获胜

第三种情况假设开放模型变得与专有模型一样强大且易于使用。 较低的成本将鼓励企业更广泛地部署人工智能，更多的工作负载在自己的数据中心或本地设备上运行，而不是集中式云服务。

这将使企业硬件、安全软件和所谓的边缘计算设备的制造商受益，这些设备在更靠近用户的地方运行较小的系统。

摩根士丹利策略师表示，微软在这个世界上仍然会表现出色。 但新的赢家将是中国的人工智能实验室和中国的科技巨头，如 MiniMax、Z.ai、阿里巴巴和腾讯。

戴尔、惠普和苹果也将在这种情况下蓬勃发展，因为它们专注于制造可以运行人工智能模型和服务的设备，更接近最终用户。 哦，Nvidia 在这里再次获胜。

不断的赢家

尽管结果截然不同，摩根士丹利还是发现了一些明显的常数。

您已经发现了最明显的赢家：Nvidia 似乎是所有三种情况中最大的受益者之一，这反映出无论哪种类型的软件获胜，对人工智能服务器和网络的持续需求。

云巨头也占据显着地位，尽管它们的排名会根据专有模式还是开放模式占据上风而变化。 微软在开放模式中脱颖而出，而如果专有模式保持主导地位或市场采用混合模式，亚马逊和谷歌将表现最强。

摩根士丹利更广泛的结论是，关于哪种类型的人工智能模型最终获胜的争论可能没有许多投资者想象的那么重要。

如果人工智能的采用继续加速，那么为其提供基础设施的公司几乎在任何未来都可能繁荣发展。
